result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both emails are accurate and honest: each gives the date, the price, the card charge, the Settings > Billing cancel path and the 60-day read-only period with CSV export, with no threats or invented perks. B is tighter, and its preview line puts the charge and the cancel deadline in front of skimmers. A has a redundant line ('If you've been sending invoices…') and a longer close that promises replies reach 'a real person', which the facts don't support. A's note catches a real problem B missed: Nov 9 is a Monday in 2026, not a Sunday, so the date should be confirmed before sending. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both emails clearly state the date, the $12/month charge to the signup card, the Settings > Billing cancel path and the 60-day read-only period with CSV export, without using deletion as a threat or inventing anything. A is slightly tighter and has a shorter close, while B adds a redundant line and a reply-to-a-person paragraph. B wins because its notes catch a real problem: Nov 9, 2026 is a Monday, not a Sunday. Sending the email as written would put a wrong weekday in the subject line.
